deep.reconstruction:
Context: the page is not Riemann's own work. It continues the editor's 'Anmerkungen des Herausgebers' to Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe' (published 1867, Werke 1876). It holds the end of note (3) and a further note, probably (5), on Riemann's Art. 13 example Σ sin(n! x π).

A. End of note (3), on the proof in Art. 9 (localisation via Riemann's second integral F).
- The editor argues that λ must also be assumed 2π-periodic.
- Counterexample: take F(t) − C't − A t²/2 = const (the 't/2' in the transcription is probably 't'). Take λ(t) = (x−t)³ (sign ±).
- Then the final integral (1/2π)∫ F(t) λ(t) d²/dt²[sin((2n+1)(x−t)/2)/sin((x−t)/2)] dt does not tend to 0. Integrating by parts leaves boundary terms that do not cancel when λ is not periodic.
- Conversely, if λ is periodic, the vanishing follows by carrying out the second t-differentiation of the Dirichlet kernel and applying Satz 3 of Art. 8. Satz 3 says μ²∫F cos μ(x−a) λ → 0. The argument is the same as in note (2) (previous page).
- Only the remark is on the page; no computation is shown.

B. Note on Σ_{n≥1} sin(n! x π).
Riemann had listed (e − e⁻¹)/4 among the irrational x for which this series converges. The editor says this is wrongly listed ('wohl mit Unrecht').

Case x = sinh(1)/2 = (1/2) Σ_m 1/(2m+1)!. Take n odd.
- n! x = (1/2)[Σ_{2m+1≤n} n!/(2m+1)! + 1/((n+1)(n+2)) + 1/((n+1)…(n+4)) + …].
- Every integer term n!/(2m+1)! with 2m+1 < n is even, and the last one is 1. So the integer part is even + 1 (the editor writes it as '…+ n(n−1) + 1').
- Hence sin(n! x π) = ±cos((π/2)r_n) with r_n = 1/((n+1)(n+2)) + … → 0.
- So |term| → 1, the general term does not tend to 0, and the series diverges.

Case x = sinh 1 = (e − e⁻¹)/2 = Σ 1/(2m+1)!.
- n odd: the integer part of n! x is odd. So sin(n! x π) = −sin(π[1/((n+1)(n+2)) + …]).
  - These terms are eventually all negative and of size ~ −π/n².
  - The odd-indexed subseries converges absolutely.
- n even: the integer part is even (the term n!/(n−1)! = n is even). So sin(n! x π) = sin(π[1/(n+1) + 1/((n+1)(n+2)(n+3)) + …]) ~ π/(n+1).
  - The even-indexed subseries diverges like the harmonic series.
- Hence the whole series diverges.

Case x = sin 1 = Σ (−1)^m/(2m+1)!. Write the index as 2n or 2n+1.
- Index 2n: (2n)! x = (even integer) + (−1)^n [1/(2n+1) − 1/((2n+1)(2n+2)(2n+3)) + …].
  - Hence sin((2n)! x π) = (−1)^n sin(π(1/(2n+1) − …)).
  - These terms alternate in sign and decrease in size (~π/(2n+1)), so the subseries converges by Leibniz.
- Index 2n+1: (2n+1)! x = (integer ≡ (−1)^n, i.e. odd) + (−1)^{n+1}[1/((2n+2)(2n+3)) − …].
  - Hence sin = (−1)^n sin(π(1/((2n+2)(2n+3)) − …)) = O(1/n²).
  - This subseries converges absolutely.
- The interleaving of a convergent and an absolutely convergent series converges. So Σ sin(n! sin1 π) converges.

Margin: the series for e^x, e^{−x} and (1/2)(e^x − e^{−x}) = x + x³/3! + x⁵/5! + …, then evaluated at x = 1.
errors: Margin: the last line '= 1 + x³/3! + x⁵/5! + …' should read 1 + 1/3! + 1/5! + … (evaluation at x = 1). This is a notational slip.
In the even-index formula for sin 1 the author writes sin(π(1/(2n+1) − …)) and claims the terms decrease. This is true for n ≥ 1, but no justification is given. It is minor.
In note (3), F(t) − C' t/2 − A t²/2 is probably C' t (as in note (2) on the previous page); this is either a transcription or a writing slip.
The statement 'sin(n!xπ) = ±cos(π/2(...))' uses a sign that depends on the parity of (n!x's integer part − 1)/2. This is fine, since only the absolute value → 1 matters.
The note-(3) claims (counterexample and fix) are asserted, not carried out on the page.

results.what: Σ sin(n! x π) diverges for x = (e − e⁻¹)/4 (general term does not → 0), correcting a value Riemann listed among points of convergence
results.modern_name: Factorial-series / Liouville-type analysis of convergence of Σ sin(n! π x) (Riemann's example in Art. 13)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (example, 1854/1867); the correction is due to the editors (Dedekind/Weber) in the Werke notes

results.what: Σ sin(n! x π) diverges for x = sinh 1 (odd terms O(1/n²), even terms ~ π/n)
results.modern_name: Elementary parity analysis of n!·(Taylor series of sinh 1)

results.what: Σ sin(n! x π) converges for x = sin 1 (alternating even-index part plus absolutely convergent odd-index part)
results.modern_name: Leibniz test applied to Riemann's example
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (value sin 1 listed in Art. 13); verification by the editors

results.what: Remark that λ must be assumed 2π-periodic in the proof of Art. 9 (localisation), with counterexample F quadratic, λ = (x−t)³
results.modern_name: Riemann localisation principle via the second integral; correction of a hypothesis

deep.surprise_reason: This is an editorial note, not original Riemann mathematics. It checks and corrects examples in Riemann's published Habilitationsschrift with elementary parity arguments on factorial series. It has some editorial-historical interest, but the mathematics is routine.

checkable.sympy: [(sum(factorial(n)/factorial(2*m+1) for m in range(0,(n+1)//2)) % 2) for n in [5,7,9,11]]
checkable.asserts: for odd n the integer part of n!·sinh(1) is odd (each entry equals 1)
for odd n, |sin(n! x π)| ≈ 1 at x = (e − 1/e)/4, so the series diverges
for even n, sin(n! sinh1 π) ≈ π n/(n+1) · 1/n, i.e. n·term → π (harmonic divergence)
for odd n, n²·sin(n! sinh1 π) → −π (negative, absolutely summable)
sin((2k)! sin1 π) ≈ (−1)^k π/(2k+1): alternating and decreasing

transcription_corrections: 'Dagegen läßt sich das Enden der Unendlichkeitsstellen der Function von λ(x)' is probably 'Dagegen lässt sich bei Erfüllung der Periodicitätsbedingung von λ(x)' (or similar).
'wie in der Anmerkung (*)' likely reads 'wie in der Anmerkung (2)'.
The note heading '(*) p. [?]' is probably '(5) p.( )'.
'ist nicht mit Unrecht unter den Werthen' should be 'ist wohl (nur) mit Unrecht unter den Werthen'. The argument shows divergence, so the sense is 'wrongly listed'.
'gesetzt[?] für welche die Reihe … convergirt[?]': the context requires convergence, and the reading 'angegeben/gesetzt … convergirt' is plausible.
'F(t) − C' t/2' is probably 'F(t) − C' t' (cf. note (2): Φ = F − C'x + A₀ x²/2; the sign of A likewise).
In the x = sin 1 lines the brace content is '{… + (−1)^n/(2n+1) …}' with an even integer before it.
Margin last line: '= 1 + 1/3! + 1/5! + …' (value at x = 1), not x³, x⁵.
